faq.q: What is the origin of Abdo?
faq.a: The recorded form is Arabic in structure and is used as a familiar/regional personal-name form.
Yes. The recorded form عَبْدُو is related to Arabic عبد, though the exact regional morphology varies.

faq.q: What is the root of Abdo?
faq.a: The form is related to the Arabic root ع ب د (ʿ-b-d), associated with servitude and worship.
Abdo is used in Muslim naming contexts, but the recorded form does not literally include the divine name Allah.
This record does not establish Abdo as an explicitly named Qur'anic person; Arabic origin alone is not proof of scriptural status.

faq.a: In Urdu it is written عبدو and can be glossed as بندہ or خادم; “اللہ کا” is not literal in the form.
The supplied “ab-do” is an approximate pronunciation; local pronunciation varies.

faq.a: The record classifies Abdo as masculine, consistent with common usage; regional frequency data is not supplied.
